## Architecture (SlideRule)

reference = a source-level type reference; use = a source-level member access; construct = a source-level object creation (`new`, including target-typed `new()`); inject = a source-level constructor-parameter dependency (primary constructors included); catch = a source-level `catch` clause (a bare `catch` counts as `System.Exception`); expose = a public signature position (return, parameter, or property/field/event type) on a public member of an externally visible type. Expand any rule ID with `sliderule explain <rule-id>` for its reason and fix.

registered = named in a source-level container registration (`AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient`/`TryAdd*`/`AddHostedService`/`AddDbContext`/`AddDbContextPool`/`AddHttpClient<TClient>`, or a `ServiceDescriptor` added to the collection), directly or through a wrapper declared in the solution; keyed-service registrations, assembly scanning, factory internals, wrappers compiled into packages and framework defaults are not seen.

### Rules
- `di/construct-via-container` — Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not construct types implementing `IPartnerClient`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/dependency-injection/guidelines>.
- `http/reuse-httpclient` — Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not construct `HttpClient`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/fundamentals/networking/http/httpclient-guidelines>.
- `di/no-service-locator` — Types, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Host.*`, must not use `IServiceProvider.GetService()`, `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetService()` or `ServiceProviderServiceExtensions.GetRequiredService()`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/dependency-injection/guidelines>.
- `di/no-buildserviceprovider` — Types must not use `ServiceCollectionContainerBuilderExtensions.BuildServiceProvider()`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/dependency-injection/guidelines>.
- `di/hosted-services-scope-their-work` — Types derived from `BackgroundService` must not reference `IOptionsSnapshot<TOptions>` or `IOutboxStore`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/scoped-service>.
- `di/no-captive-dependencies` — Singleton-registered types must not inject scoped-registered types or transient-registered types. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/extensions/dependency-injection/guidelines>.
- `naming/async-suffix` — Methods returning `Task`, `Task<TResult>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` declared in authored types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except overriding methods of types or interface-implementing methods of types, must be named `*Async`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/task-based-asynchronous-pattern-tap>.
- `exceptions/no-general-catch` — Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except types derived from `BackgroundService`, must not swallow `Exception`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/design-guidelines/using-standard-exception-types>.
- `async/accept-cancellation` — Methods returning `Task`, `Task<TResult>`, `ValueTask` or `ValueTask<TResult>` declared in authored types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except overriding methods of types or interface-implementing methods of types, must accept a parameter of type `CancellationToken`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/standard/asynchronous-programming-patterns/task-based-asynchronous-pattern-tap>.
- `persistence/no-mapping-attributes` — Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*` must not be attributed with `[Table]` or `[ComplexType]`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/modern-web-apps-azure/architectural-principles>.
- `contracts/no-entity-exposure` — Types in `Meridian.Interchange.*`, except types in `Meridian.Interchange.Outbox.*`, must not expose `OutboxMessage`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/architecture/microservices/microservice-ddd-cqrs-patterns/cqrs-microservice-reads>.

### Migrations
- `async/no-sync-over-async` — Some existing code here still follows the OLD pattern: A legacy manifest gateway exposes only synchronous calls, so the adapter blocks on async work. That is grandfathered debt, not house style. New code must follow: Types must not use `Task.Wait()`, `Task<TResult>.Result`, `ValueTask<TResult>.Result`, `TaskAwaiter.GetResult()`, `TaskAwaiter<TResult>.GetResult()`, `ValueTaskAwaiter.GetResult()` or `ValueTaskAwaiter<TResult>.GetResult()`. See <https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/asynchronous-programming/async-scenarios>. If you are already editing a grandfathered site and the migration is small, migrate it; otherwise do not grow the debt.
